items.claim: The row defends only the right boundary against 25:10 and leaves an equally live left-seam catchword chain with 25:8 entirely undisclosed.
items.evidence: 25:8 (לָרִ֗ב ... רֵעֶֽךָ) and 25:9 (רִֽ֭יבְךָ רִ֣יב ... רֵעֶ֑ךָ) share the root ריב (dispute; used twice in v9 as a cognate noun-plus-verb construction, once in v8) plus the identical word רעך ('your neighbor'), a byte-true device straddling the row's own left seam that the standing cross-seam-cohesion rule requires disclosed whatever the outcome. The same writer pass explicitly disclosed the weaker, non-adjacent version of this same רעך echo (25:8-9 vs 25:17) inside its own companion row, so the methodology was available but not applied to this row's immediate left boundary.

items.claim: The exclusivity claim that זהב 'occurs nowhere else in this part' is false; the token also occurs at 27:21, inside P11 (25:1-27:27).
items.evidence: sweep.py --skel זהב returns 7 verses book-wide, 3 of them inside P11: Prov.25.11, Prov.25.12, and Prov.27.21 (מַצְרֵ֣ף לַ֭כֶּסֶף וְכ֣וּר לַזָּהָ֑ב ...). 27:21 even repeats the same particle-less metal-image-set-beside-an-abstract-quality construction the row calls unique to the 11-12 pair, though 27:21 is not adjacent to them. The adjacency-plus-exact-repetition case for clustering 25:11-12 itself still stands, but the unqualified 'nowhere else in this part' sentence is a false digit claim and needs correction; the rejected_alternative's narrower 'nowhere else ADJACENT in the part' phrasing is the only version that survives the sweep.
tier_citations: sweep.py --skel זהב (skeleton tier: 3 verses in P11 / 7 book-wide)

items.claim: The claimed skeleton sweep of 25:17 against its neighbors 'comes back empty' is false: 25:16 and 25:17 both carry the root שבע inside a matching פן-clause warning template.
items.evidence: sweep.py --skel שבע returns 25 verses book-wide, including the consecutive pair Prov.25.16 (תִּ֝שְׂבָּעֶ֗נּוּ) and Prov.25.17 (יִ֝שְׂבָּעֲךָ֗) -- the same root inside the same 'lest you/he be sated...' frame. Because שבע recurs in 25 verses book-wide it does not clear the C5 bounded-catchword bar for proverb_cluster, so single_proverb likely still holds, but the row's affirmative 'comes back empty' claim is the opposite of the tool's output and must be corrected to a root-commonality argument rather than an absence claim.
tier_citations: sweep.py --skel שבע (skeleton tier: 25 verses book-wide incl. Prov.25.16, Prov.25.17)

items.claim: The 25:19/25:20 ביום overlap is correctly treated as a common temporal collocation rather than bounded cohesion, and the row's own cited comparanda check out.
items.evidence: oshb:Prov.25.13 and oshb:Prov.27.10 both carry the same ביום-plus-noun collocation the row cites as recurring texture; oshb:Prov.25.18 and oshb:Prov.25.19 share no skeleton vocabulary, so the left boundary is likewise clean. The 25-26 zone's dense implied-simile texture (18, 19, and 20 all juxtapose images without a comparison particle) makes that shared FORM a book-wide default rather than bounded cohesion, consistent with the row's own phrase-extension-trap framing and the atomic-default guidance for this zone.

items.claim: The rejected_alternative's parenthetical '(see that row)' is a positional cross-row reference rather than a verse-anchored one, a register-purge violation even though the verse (25:19) is already named in the same clause.
items.evidence: Row prose reads 'No merge with 25:19 (see that row) or 25:21 ... was warranted.' The standing register rule requires cross-row references to be verse-anchored only, with no positional or file-structure references to other rows in the corpus; 'that row' names the corpus artifact, not the text. The substantive content is otherwise sound: pmarks_Prov.json confirms Prov.25.20 = [PE] (single-witness, tier-3), and the row correctly frames it as trailing (post-verse) corroboration for its own right boundary rather than a driver.

items.claim: The כי-clause pronoun in 25:22 genuinely depends on 25:21's enemy referent, and the front-seam petuchah at 25:20 is accurately disclosed as corroboration for the cluster's own left boundary.
items.evidence: oshb:Prov.25.22 carries עַל רֹאשׁ֑וֹ ('on his head') -- the 3ms suffix on רֹאשׁ֑וֹ ('his head') has no antecedent within v22 itself and requires v21's שֹׂ֭נַאֲךָ ('the one hating you') to resolve, a genuine syntactic dependency rather than a shared-theme cluster. pmarks_Prov.json confirms Prov.25.20 = [PE] (single-witness, tier-3), correctly disclosed as the front-seam mark bounding the cluster's own start; no shared vocabulary ties v22 to v23, so the right boundary needs no further defense.

items.claim: The intra-verse כבד wordplay is byte-accurate and the 'no skeleton token with 25:26 or 25:28' claim checks out; the 25:16 honey echo is correctly disclosed as texture, not a driver.
items.evidence: oshb:Prov.25.27 carries both כְּבֹדָ֣ם and כָּבֽוֹד from the root כבד (byte-collated); its token set has no overlap with oshb:Prov.25.26 (מעין / מקור / צדיק / רשע) or oshb:Prov.25.28 (עיר / חומה / רוח), confirming the clean isolation claimed on both sides. The 25:16 honey/אכל echo is real but distant and is disclosed as texture rather than adopted as a driver, matching the standing cross-seam-cohesion disclosure rule.

items.claim: The 26:4-5 identical closing phrase and the flatly reversed governing imperative are byte-confirmed, matching the owner-ratified exemplar cluster for this collection.
items.evidence: oshb:Prov.26.4 (כְּ֭סִיל כְּאִוַּלְתּ֑וֹ) and oshb:Prov.26.5 (כְ֭סִיל כְּאִוַּלְתּ֑וֹ) collate at byte tier as the identical closing phrase; the governing verbs תַּ֣עַן (with the preceding אל) in v4 and עֲנֵ֣ה in v5 are a genuine flat reversal, byte-confirmed against source. The rejected_alternative properly addresses both the independent-sayings rival and the harmonizing-reading rival as the strongest real challengers, matching the mandated-rival disclosure for this pair.
